name: Float on your back
blurb: Sounds trivial, saves lives. A relaxed back float lets you rest indefinitely and is the first thing to do if you get into trouble — but almost everyone tenses up and sinks their hips on the first try.
steps: Start in shallow water where you can stand up easily, so failing costs nothing.
Lie back with your ears in the water and your chin up, looking straight at the ceiling or sky.
Push your hips and belly up towards the surface — this is the part everyone gets wrong.
Spread your arms and legs wide into a star to increase stability.
Breathe slowly and fully. Full lungs float; empty lungs sink, so keep more air in than feels natural.
Practise recovering to standing, then float progressively longer, then try it in deeper water.
tips: Tension is what sinks you. If your hips drop, you are holding your breath or curling up.
Salt water floats you far more easily than fresh — do not judge your ability from a holiday in the sea.
proof: Five relaxed minutes floating in deep water, hands and feet still.
